method: Web research against museum sites and reputable listings press (Sept 2026); every title, venue, and full date range verified against an official or press page, or corroborated across multiple sources. Shows that closed since the last refresh were dropped (Whitney Biennial 2026, Greater New York 2026, Marcel Duchamp and Frida and Diego at MoMA, Revolution! at the Met, The Seventh AIM Biennial, Sara Flores at White Cube, Basquiat x Banksy and State Fairs and Dear America and Isaac Julien and Here: Pride and Belonging in DC, Fratino and Matisse and the Sondheim finalists and Douriean Fletcher and Fantastic Realities in Baltimore, Freedom Dreams at the Barnes, Vincent's Path to Fame and Ed van der Elsken and Made in China and Judy Chicago and Rembrandt & Life and Eko in Amsterdam, Marina Abramovic at the Gropius Bau, Lee Bul at M+, the Museo Jumex football show, Macunaima e Duwid at the Pinacoteca, Waldmuller at the National Gallery). Marcel Duchamp is retained under its new Philadelphia Museum of Art dates. Many fall openings were added: Taryn Simon and the Roy Lichtenstein retrospective, Krasner and Pollock at the Met, Brancusi at MoMA, Art of Manga and the Pearlman Collection at the Brooklyn Museum, Siena bronzes at the Frick, Willem de Kooning and the Van Gogh Museum's Yoshitoshi and Whistler shows, Chez Matisse, the Foam and Eye reopenings, Do Ho Suh in Seoul, Zurbaran and Mary Cassatt in Paris, Renoir and Love in London, and more.

exhibitions.title: Guggenheim Pop: 1960 to Now
exhibitions.artist: Warhol, Lichtenstein, Oldenburg, Hamilton, Chryssa, and others
exhibitions.blurb: Pop art from the Guggenheim's collection spirals up the rotunda alongside a Kusama Infinity Mirror Room and recent acquisitions that interrogate Pop's legacy.
exhibitions.note: Rotunda closes when Taryn Simon takes it over on Sep 18; the Pop galleries stay open.

exhibitions.title: Taryn Simon: Father Country I Do Love You
exhibitions.blurb: The first rotunda takeover by a photography-based artist fills the spiral with new photographs, text, video, and sculpture in a single interactive installation.
exhibitions.note: Billed as the largest debut of new work ever staged at the Guggenheim.

exhibitions.title: Rembrandt's Lions: Art and Exile in the Dutch Republic
exhibitions.blurb: The Morgan gathers Rembrandt's celebrated lion drawings and the world of the Dutch Republic around them - intimate sheets by a master observer of living things.
exhibitions.note: Final weeks; closes Oct 4.

exhibitions.title: Modernity and Opulence: Women of the Wiener Werkstätte
exhibitions.blurb: For the first time, the lasting contributions of the Jewish women who shaped the Wiener Werkstätte's modernist design language, as artists and as patrons.
exhibitions.note: Organized with Vienna's MAK museum.

exhibitions.title: Octopus & Others: Acts of Collaboration & Poetics
exhibitions.artist: Group exhibition, inspired by Papo Colo
exhibitions.blurb: Revisits Exit Art co-founder Papo Colo's 1982 courtyard performance Octopus: An Act of Sculpture as a launchpad for new collaborative and poetic works by contemporary artists.
exhibitions.note: Anchored by a recent gift of panels from Colo's original Octopus.

exhibitions.title: Teddy Sandoval and the Butch Gardens School of Art
exhibitions.blurb: The first major survey of Teddy Sandoval (1949-1995), a Los Angeles artist whose ceramics, mail art, and painting probed gender and identity with humor and political nerve.
exhibitions.note: Traveled from the Williams College Museum of Art.

exhibitions.title: Anicka Yi: Message from the Mud
exhibitions.blurb: Yi's first large-scale outdoor project stages a fictional archaeological dig - twenty living Winogradsky columns culturing Storm King's own pond mud into slow paintings.
exhibitions.note: Storm King, New Windsor - Hudson Valley day trip.

exhibitions.title: Iris van Herpen: Sculpting the Senses
exhibitions.blurb: The North American debut of this retrospective gathers more than 140 haute couture creations by the Dutch designer alongside the scientific and artistic references that inspired them.
exhibitions.note: Separately ticketed, timed entry recommended.

exhibitions.title: Art of Manga
exhibitions.blurb: Original artwork spanning the history of manga makes its East Coast debut in the Museum's Great Hall, with pages tied to Inuyasha, JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, Ooku, and One Piece.
exhibitions.note: Separately ticketed; expect crowds on weekends.

exhibitions.title: Cézanne to Modigliani: Gifts of Modern Art from the Pearlman Collection
exhibitions.artist: Cézanne, Modigliani, van Gogh, and others
exhibitions.blurb: More than fifty modern European works from the late 19th to mid-20th century, drawn from the celebrated collection of Henry and Rose Pearlman.
exhibitions.note: Includes a strong group of Cézanne watercolors.

exhibitions.title: Buddha and Shiva, Lotus and Dragon: Celebrating 70 Years of Asia Society and the Rockefeller Legacy
exhibitions.blurb: Seventy masterworks in bronze, ceramic, and metal assembled by John D. Rockefeller 3rd, marking Asia Society's 70th anniversary.
exhibitions.note: Museum is free on Fridays.

exhibitions.title: Roy Lichtenstein: Like New
exhibitions.blurb: More than 130 works trace Lichtenstein from the early 1940s to the 1990s, reframing him around copying, enlargement, and circulation rather than Pop-era surface.
exhibitions.note: Curated by Meg Onli with guest curator Alex Da Corte; includes a recreation of his 1962 breakout show.

exhibitions.title: The Lost World: The Art of Minnie Evans
exhibitions.blurb: The visionary North Carolina artist returns to the Whitney more than fifty years after it organized her first solo show, with densely patterned drawings of a paradise garden.
exhibitions.note: Eighth-floor galleries.

exhibitions.title: Coumba Samba: Stars and Stripes
exhibitions.blurb: The first solo museum presentation of the Senegalese American artist is an immersive installation examining nuclear power and the African resource extraction that fed it.
exhibitions.note: First-floor gallery, free with the lobby.

exhibitions.title: Siena: The Art of Bronze, 1450-1500
exhibitions.artist: Francesco di Giorgio, Vecchietta, and others
exhibitions.blurb: The first exhibition on Siena as a center of Renaissance bronze, bringing together some forty works, most never before shown outside Tuscany.
exhibitions.note: In the newly renovated Frick's special-exhibition galleries.

exhibitions.title: Krasner and Pollock: Past Continuous
exhibitions.blurb: The first major New York show devoted to either artist in more than two decades sets the two painters' careers side by side as a continuous conversation.
exhibitions.note: The Tisch Galleries; timed tickets with admission.

exhibitions.title: Brancusi: The Artist and His Studio
exhibitions.blurb: Brancusi's sculpture seen through the lens of his Paris studio, with rarely lent works from the Centre Pompidou joining MoMA's deep holdings.
exhibitions.note: Special exhibition ticket required.

exhibitions.title: American Icon: The US Flag in Art
exhibitions.artist: Jasper Johns, Gordon Parks, Juan Sánchez, and others
exhibitions.blurb: More than thirty works from the National Gallery's collection trace how artists have saluted, reworked, and interrogated the flag.
exhibitions.note: East Building Concourse; free, no passes.

exhibitions.title: Sky Hopinka: Kicking the Clouds
exhibitions.blurb: Through photographs, poems, and film, Hopinka connects family, language, place, and lived Indigenous experience.
exhibitions.note: West Building, Ground Floor, Gallery G22; free.

exhibitions.title: Adam Pendleton: Love, Queen
exhibitions.blurb: New and recent paintings plus a video work wrapping the second-floor inner ring - Pendleton's first Washington solo, mounted for the museum's 50th anniversary.
exhibitions.note: On view into 2027; free, like all Smithsonian museums.

exhibitions.title: Nick Cave: Mammoth
exhibitions.blurb: A monumental new commission: visitors walk among the fantastical remains of ancient creatures, Cave's excavation of American memory at a fraught Smithsonian moment.
exhibitions.note: New commission for SAAM; free.

exhibitions.title: Photographic Memory: Fifty Years of Photography at the National Portrait Gallery
exhibitions.blurb: A hundred-plus works from daguerreotype to digital, marking fifty years of the museum collecting the photographed face.
exhibitions.note: Semiquincentennial season; free.

exhibitions.title: The Spirit of Invention: Patent Office and Patentees
exhibitions.blurb: Portraits and objects celebrate the inventors tied to the Portrait Gallery's historic home, once the United States Patent Office building.
exhibitions.note: First Floor East galleries; free.

exhibitions.title: Saodat Ismailova: Melted into the Sun
exhibitions.blurb: The Uzbek artist's first major US museum presentation weaves film and installation around Central Asian myth, memory, and landscape.
exhibitions.note: Arthur M. Sackler Gallery, Gallery 28; free.

exhibitions.title: From the Louvre: Masterpieces of Islamic Art
exhibitions.blurb: Twenty-six works from the Louvre's Department of Islamic Art, from ceramics and metalwork to manuscript pages, on a rare visit to Washington.
exhibitions.note: Free general admission.

exhibitions.title: Routed West: Twentieth-Century African American Quilts in California
exhibitions.venue: National Museum of Women in the Arts
exhibitions.blurb: More than eighty quilts trace the Second Great Migration west, blending record-keeping, resourcefulness, and improvisation.
exhibitions.note: Ticketed general admission, not free.

exhibitions.title: Avery, Gottlieb & Rothko: By the Sea
exhibitions.artist: Milton Avery, Adolph Gottlieb, Mark Rothko
exhibitions.blurb: About ninety works follow the friendship of three painters and the coastal summers in Gloucester, Massachusetts, that shaped their art.
exhibitions.note: Ticketed general admission.

exhibitions.title: Matisse and Martinique: Portraits and Poetry
exhibitions.blurb: A focused chapter of the BMA's unrivalled Matisse holdings, pairing portraiture with poetry inspired by his 1930 Martinique visit.
exhibitions.note: Cone Collection country; last of the BMA's 2026 Matisse trio still on view.

exhibitions.title: Raúl de Nieves: and imagine you are here
exhibitions.blurb: De Nieves' shimmering beaded figures and stained-glass-like panels transform the BMA's East Lobby into a processional fantasy, on long-term view.
exhibitions.note: East Lobby commission; free admission.

exhibitions.title: Flashback: Two Centuries of Baltimore Photography
exhibitions.artist: A. Aubrey Bodine, Devin Allen, Elle Pérez, and others
exhibitions.blurb: The first comprehensive survey of Baltimore's role in photography's development - more than 200 works by 90 named artists across 185 years.
exhibitions.note: Free admission.

exhibitions.title: Divine Inspiration: The Legacy of the St. Francis Missal
exhibitions.blurb: A rare showing of the fragile 12th-century missal that Franciscans revere as a touch relic of St. Francis, with eighteen related objects marking the 800th anniversary of his death.
exhibitions.note: Free admission.

exhibitions.title: A Nation of Artists
exhibitions.blurb: A thousand-plus portraits, sculptures and photographs spanning three centuries of American art - a blockbuster split across two museums on the Parkway.
exhibitions.note: Dual-venue with PAFA; PAFA's run extends about two months longer.

exhibitions.title: Fred Wilson: The Master Plan
exhibitions.blurb: Twenty-two photogravures reproducing museum floor-plan maps - a wry meditation on how institutions frame art, shown alongside A Nation of Artists.
exhibitions.note: Works on Paper Gallery, Historic Landmark Building.

exhibitions.title: Sky Hopinka: Red Metal Dust
exhibitions.blurb: Eleven immersive panels layering landscape photographs over copper sheets - a commissioned meditation on America's history with Indigenous peoples, filling the Annenberg Court.
exhibitions.note: Annenberg Court commission.

exhibitions.title: Noguchi to Asawa: Designing Postwar America
exhibitions.blurb: Sculpture and design by two generations of Japanese American artists, from Noguchi's lamps and playgrounds to Asawa's looped-wire forms.
exhibitions.note: Roberts Gallery.

exhibitions.title: Marcel Duchamp
exhibitions.blurb: The first North American Duchamp retrospective in over fifty years lands in the city with the world's deepest Duchamp holdings, spanning six decades and every medium.
exhibitions.note: Dorrance Galleries; the show ran at MoMA earlier in 2026.

exhibitions.title: Workshop of the World: Arts and Crafts in Philadelphia
exhibitions.blurb: More than 250 objects - ceramics, furniture, metalwork, stained glass - spotlight Philadelphia's Arts and Crafts movement, including Samuel Yellin and Violet Oakley.
exhibitions.note: Closes Oct 11; timed to the museum's 150th.

exhibitions.title: Jesse Krimes: Elegy Quilts
exhibitions.blurb: Quilts made from materials contributed by currently and formerly incarcerated people explore memories of home, shown with a new Mural Arts collaboration.
exhibitions.note: Pair with the museum's Contemporary Tapestry survey next door.

exhibitions.title: Ali Banisadr: Temple of the Mind
exhibitions.blurb: The AKG's first artist collection intervention - Banisadr threads his own work through the permanent galleries alongside his picks from Hiroshige to Goya.
exhibitions.note: Hemicycle Gallery and throughout the Wilmers Building.

exhibitions.title: Ragnar Kjartansson: Politics of the Obvious
exhibitions.blurb: Six immersive video and performance installations by the Icelandic artist, half making their US museum debut, turning familiar gestures into extended meditations on aspiration and precarity.
exhibitions.note: Several works are durational video loops; budget extra time to sit with them.

exhibitions.title: Natvar Bhavsar: Free Yourself
exhibitions.blurb: Fifty years of the Indian-born painter's dry-pigment abstractions, split between the AKG's works on paper and monumental canvases at the University at Buffalo Art Galleries.
exhibitions.note: Two-venue presentation with UB Art Galleries.

exhibitions.title: Kindred: Works from the Burchfield Penney and Seneca-Iroquois National Museum Collections
exhibitions.blurb: A collaboration with the Seneca-Iroquois National Museum on how artists preserve, reinterpret, and evolve cultural practices across both collections.
exhibitions.note: On view at the Burchfield Penney Off Center at K Art, 808 Main Street.

exhibitions.title: A VAST, tiny WORLD: Burchfield's Insects & Spiders
exhibitions.blurb: Burchfield's lifelong fascination with the insect world, from field-journal studies to the vibrating, haloed creatures of his late watercolors.
exhibitions.note: Curated by Burchfield scholar Nancy Weekly.

exhibitions.title: Carel Visser in the Rijksmuseum Gardens
exhibitions.blurb: Monumental steel sculptures by the Netherlands' foremost twentieth-century sculptor, gathered outdoors for the first time.
exhibitions.note: The gardens are free to visit even without a museum ticket.

exhibitions.title: Willem de Kooning at Work
exhibitions.blurb: More than 120 paintings, drawings, and sculptures follow the Rotterdam-born painter's decades-long push toward a new kind of American abstraction.
exhibitions.note: Philips Wing; timed entry recommended.

exhibitions.title: Yayoi Kusama: Retrospective
exhibitions.blurb: Seven decades of dots, nets and mirror rooms in a full retrospective - Amsterdam's big autumn ticket, worth planning a trip around.
exhibitions.note: Just opened; book a timed slot for the Infinity Mirror Rooms.

exhibitions.title: Kho Liang Ie: Mid-Century Modernist
exhibitions.blurb: The first major retrospective in over fifty years of the designer behind Schiphol's interiors and landmark Dutch furniture.
exhibitions.note: Includes a reconstruction of part of his 1971 Stedelijk exhibition.

exhibitions.title: Yoshitoshi: Master of the Moon
exhibitions.blurb: All 100 prints of Yoshitoshi's celebrated series One Hundred Aspects of the Moon, made 1885-1890, showing warriors, lovers, ghosts and poets under moonlight.
exhibitions.note: Print Room; a companion to the museum's Japanese holdings.

exhibitions.title: Whistler: Dandy and Disruptor
exhibitions.blurb: The first retrospective in the Netherlands of the American expatriate who argued that a picture should evoke a mood, not tell a story.
exhibitions.note: Timed entry - book the museum slot well ahead.

exhibitions.title: Chez Matisse: Masterpieces from Centre Pompidou
exhibitions.blurb: More than thirty Matisse paintings, sculptures and prints from the Centre Pompidou, set among contemporaries and followers from Picasso to Rothko.
exhibitions.note: Organized with the Centre Pompidou during its long closure.

exhibitions.title: The Land of Chocolate Sprinkles: Building a New World Together
exhibitions.blurb: The Congolese collective CATPC debuts in Amsterdam with sculptures made from cocoa, palm oil, and sugar confronting plantation economics.
exhibitions.note: Proceeds from related sales help the artists buy back exhausted plantation land.

exhibitions.title: Nadav Kander: The Edge of Things
exhibitions.blurb: Four decades of the photographer's work - portraits of Obama and David Lynch, atmospheric landscapes, and studies of the body - in one survey.
exhibitions.note: Opens alongside new shows by Hailun Ma and Keerthana Kunnath.

exhibitions.title: Ulrich Seidl: Über das Leben, die Liebe und den Tod
exhibitions.blurb: Early, little-known and newly commissioned work by the Austrian filmmaker, confronting visitors with the lives of seemingly ordinary people.
exhibitions.note: Reopens Eye's temporary exhibition space; across the IJ by free ferry.

exhibitions.title: Queer Amsterdam, the Pink City
exhibitions.blurb: A long-running exhibition on the history of Amsterdam's LGBTQIA+ community - love, exclusion, courage and hard-won freedom - mounted for WorldPride 2026.
exhibitions.note: On Dam Square, beside the Palace.

exhibitions.title: DISCO: More Than Beats and Glitter
exhibitions.blurb: Disco as a cultural movement built on freedom, inclusivity and self-expression, told through fashion, sound, photography and design.
exhibitions.note: Title translated from the Dutch; long run into next summer.

exhibitions.title: Diana Blok: Time Tells
exhibitions.blurb: A small side-gallery photography show on family history and memory, shown in the museum's Kunstkabinet.
exhibitions.note: Compact; part of the Jewish Cultural Quarter.

exhibitions.title: Martine Gutierrez: Wunderkind
exhibitions.blurb: The American artist's shape-shifting self-portraiture takes over two seventeenth-century canal houses on the Keizersgracht.
exhibitions.note: Amsterdam's photography jewel box; closes Oct 18.

exhibitions.title: Glass, Made in Antiquity
exhibitions.blurb: Over 200 ancient glass objects examined with nuclear-reactor and X-ray techniques, shown alongside two contemporary glass artists.
exhibitions.note: Final months; closes Nov 1.

exhibitions.title: Ana Mendieta
exhibitions.blurb: Her first comprehensive UK exhibition in over a decade: over 150 works including the iconic Silueta series, newly remastered films, early paintings and late sculpture.
exhibitions.note: First UK survey in over a decade.

exhibitions.title: Julio Le Parc: Light. Colour. Action.
exhibitions.blurb: Interactive installations, mirrored kinetic sculptures and op-art canvases from the 1950s to the 2010s - a posthumous retrospective, as Le Parc died days before it opened.
exhibitions.note: On view for nearly a year.

exhibitions.title: Richard Dadd: Beyond Bedlam
exhibitions.blurb: A survey of the Victorian painter of obsessive fairy miniatures, most made inside Bethlem and Broadmoor - strange, minute, unforgettable.
exhibitions.note: Closes Oct 25; book weekends ahead.

exhibitions.title: Renoir and Love
exhibitions.blurb: Around forty-five works focus on Renoir's crucial years, mid-1860s to mid-1880s, with the Musée d'Orsay's Dance at the Moulin de la Galette shown in the UK for the first time.
exhibitions.note: The most significant Renoir show in the UK in twenty years; ticketed.

exhibitions.title: Affinités: Les merveilles des arts de l'Islam aux Objets d'art
exhibitions.blurb: Around fifty Islamic-art objects from the ninth to seventeenth centuries placed in dialogue with the Louvre's Decorative Arts collection around light, colour, and sculpture.
exhibitions.note: In the Objets d'art galleries, Richelieu wing.

exhibitions.title: Zurbarán
exhibitions.blurb: A major retrospective of the Spanish Golden Age master, tracing his path from Caravaggesque naturalism to the still, luminous devotional pictures of his maturity.
exhibitions.note: Hall Napoléon; organized with the National Gallery, London and the Art Institute of Chicago.

exhibitions.title: Mary Cassatt: The Choice of Independence
exhibitions.blurb: The first major exhibition in France devoted to the American Impressionist who built her career in Paris and shaped what US collectors brought home.
exhibitions.note: On the museum's upper level.

exhibitions.title: Jenny Holzer: J'ai Vu
exhibitions.blurb: Monumental installations, façade projections, electronic signs and engraved stones carry Holzer's aphorisms and found language into the former railway station.
exhibitions.note: Includes projections onto the museum's historic exterior.

exhibitions.title: Ron Mueck
exhibitions.blurb: Eleven works tracing Mueck's uncanny hyperrealism, with the Japan premiere of Mass - one hundred giant skulls - and six pieces never before shown in Japan.
exhibitions.note: Closes Sep 23; open to 22:00 most nights, 53rd floor.

exhibitions.title: Mariko Mori: All That Shines
exhibitions.blurb: A three-decade retrospective of the artist's fusion of art, science and metaphysics - some eighty works across interactive installation, sculpture, video and performance.
exhibitions.note: Co-curated with the Guggenheim's Alexandra Munroe.

exhibitions.title: Ryuichi Sakamoto: seeing sound, hearing time
exhibitions.blurb: The first major European retrospective of the late composer and artist gathers seven works into five large-scale installations blurring sound, time and image.
exhibitions.note: Some rooms are darkened, immersive sound environments; allow time to sit.

exhibitions.title: Design Ah! Experience the Wonder of Everyday Design
exhibitions.artist: Group show, based on the NHK TV program
exhibitions.blurb: Twenty-one interactive stations built around everyday actions, adapted for Hong Kong from the viral Japanese children's design TV program.
exhibitions.note: Good for visiting with kids.

exhibitions.title: Myths and Monsters: The Art of Fantasy in Asia
exhibitions.blurb: From the nineteenth century to now, fantasy as a creative tool artists use to respond to shifting political conditions across Asia and beyond.
exhibitions.note: West Gallery.

exhibitions.title: Do Ho Suh
exhibitions.blurb: The artist's largest exhibition to date - more than 500 drawings, sculptures, videos and installations mapping four decades of home, memory and migration.
exhibitions.note: The Genesis Exhibition; a homecoming after Walk the House at Tate Modern.

exhibitions.title: Koo Jeong A: OUSSSMOS
exhibitions.blurb: The largest Korean survey of Koo Jeong A - around thirty-five works from the early 1990s to new commissions, spilling from gallery M2 into the lobby and the traditional-art galleries.
exhibitions.note: Opened during Seoul Art Week.

exhibitions.title: Before the Eclipse: Archaeologies of Art in Mexico
exhibitions.blurb: More than sixty artists reassess 1980s Mexico through pre-Hispanic heritage, territory, and the country's globalizing turn.
exhibitions.note: Chapultepec Park; closes Oct 18.

exhibitions.title: Richard Prince: Tell Me Everything
exhibitions.blurb: A career survey of the American artist's rephotography, jokes, and cowboys - the pictures that made appropriation a house style.
exhibitions.note: The museum reopens after an installation break with this show.

exhibitions.title: Carolina Caycedo: Confluências
exhibitions.blurb: The Colombian-American artist's work on rivers, extraction, and collective resistance, on Avenida Paulista.
exhibitions.note: Closes Oct 4; includes the live performance Atarraya in the Free Space.

exhibitions.title: Latin American Histories
exhibitions.blurb: A five-floor international group show, the anchor of MASP's year, examining how the idea of Latin America was constructed and keeps being contested.
exhibitions.note: Fills the Pietro Maria Bardi Building; allow a half day.

exhibitions.title: Via Satélite: Nam June Paik in Dialogue with Vivian Caccuri
exhibitions.blurb: A retrospective of the video-art pioneer set in conversation with Brazilian artist Vivian Caccuri's work on sound, perception and technology.
exhibitions.note: Pinacoteca Contemporânea building.

exhibitions.title: Biennale Arte 2026: In Minor Keys
exhibitions.blurb: The 61st International Art Exhibition realises the late Koyo Kouoh's 'In Minor Keys' - 110 invited participants plus a hundred national pavilions across the city and Forte Marghera.
exhibitions.note: Final weeks; allow two full days and comfortable shoes.
